title: Ercole II d'Este to his secretary Claudio Ariosti, Ferrara, 8 Jan 1547, on the rising at Genoa (Biblioteca Estense, Autografoteca Campori, Ercole II, c. 16v; catalogue 2160): key recovered from the ciphertext alone, eight cipher lines read in part (contributed by Malcolm McBratney with Claude)

documents.shelfmark: Biblioteca Estense Universitaria, Modena, Autografoteca Campori, Ercole II d'Este, sfasc. I, cc. 16-17; cipher on c. 16v, 8 lines (IIIF manifest 89e1bdc6-a46d-4627-9770-efbd17e544fb)
documents.date: Ferrara, 8 January 1547 (date line 'Ferrariae viij Jan. 1547' on c. 16v)

plaintext.source: No key, decipherment, interlinear or printed reading found (PRIOR_ART.md). The clear lines of the letter (10 above, 2 below the cipher) are the letter itself, not a decipherment.

transcription.source: Estense IIIF, native-resolution crops of c. 16v (FETCH_LOG.txt)
transcription.notes: Length: _check_profile.py --measure transcription_c16v.txt --drop-first gives 290 whitespace tokens = 276 signs (each with its raised mark; 160 marks) + 13 dots + 1 punctuation {:}; 276 counted here. decode_once.py gives 435 letters (validation.tsv). One reader (Claude Fable 5.2), one pass, blind to any key; 12 doubtful tokens marked ?. Frozen with the split before any solving (FREEZE_TX.txt). S09 mixes two signs (figure 6 and a b/f-like sign) that were not separated. Not checked by a person.

system.summary: Signs of Latin shape for consonants; the vowel after a consonant is given by a raised figure (4 a, 5 e, 6 i, 7 o, 8 u) or, on a second class of consonant signs, by a stroke (/ a, \ e, upright o); figures on the line are vowels; a bar over a consonant doubles it; d with a cross after c = 'he' (che); dots on the line are nulls; one code sign for a person (S01^4s).
system.notes: 25 sign shapes and 15 raised marks (SIGNS.md). Same family as ariosto1559 (catalogue 2159: sign plus raised vowel figure) but a different table: other sign shapes, other figure values, a bar not a ring for doubling. Weak values: raised 9 and 2 (o), S10 under a bar (ni), S02^^ (ri); no value for S12^- and the code sign S01^4s (KEY.tsv).

prior_solution.where: None found: the pages, the Estense record, Cyphersolver catalogue 2160 and targets/ (Brice Dudout's attempt in targets/ariosto1559/NOTES.md, 'Not solved'), DECODE public search, web searches, the ASMo Ambasciatori Germania inventory (first half), filodiritto.com on Este ciphers (PRIOR_ART.md). Not checked: ASMo Cancelleria, Cifrario; Cremonini 2019; HathiTrust and Google Books full text; DECODE records behind login.

conditions.human_role: Malcolm McBratney directed the work and set its rules (prior art first, transcription and key frozen before one decode, held-out lines, a separate strict judge, first pass as the figure of record, shuffle controls). Claude sessions did the transcription, key recovery, decode, judging, reading and translation. No reading by a person without AI.
tools: work/solver.py, work/solver2.py: annealing on five structural models, scored with a local Italian 5-gram model (work/build_lm.py)
shuffle.py: 5,000 shuffled keys at two seeds
models: Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic): the solver session (transcription, key recovery, decode, controls) [stated by the contributor]
Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic): the strict judge, and the session that assembled this folder, reading.md and translation.md

solution.what: Prior art before transcription: the pages, Estense record, catalogue 2160, Cyphersolver targets (Brice Dudout's 5 Nov 2026 attempt on this letter, 'Not solved', in targets/ariosto1559/NOTES.md), DECODE public search, web, ASMo inventory (PRIOR_ART.md). No key, decipherment or reading found.
Estense IIIF images of cc. 16r, 16v, 17r, 17v and native-resolution crops of the cipher on 16v (FETCH_LOG.txt). Full-size requests refused (HTTP 422); crops served.

8 cipher lines transcribed by sign shape, blind to any key: 276 signs, 160 raised marks, 13 dots; 25 sign shapes, 15 marks; 12 doubtful tokens marked. Frozen with the split BUILD = lines 1-6 (216 signs), HELD-OUT = lines 7-8 (60 signs) (FREEZE_TX.txt).
ariosto1559 (2159) key and image compared, and ercole1559, ercole1544, capilupi1545, capilupi1546, bresegno1548, francescoeste1546: other tables (PRIOR_ART.md).
Counts of signs and marks by sign (SOLVE_LOG 1): two classes of consonant signs (raised figures against strokes); S05^X always after S03; bars come with a dot.
Model A, marks ignored, 3 seeds then 4 seeds with a frequency term: collapsed or no words (SOLVE_LOG 2-3).
Model B (raised figure = vowel, free), 4 seeds x 250k: not converged, but raised 5 = e, 6 = i, 7 = o in 4 of 4 runs, 4 = a in 3 of 4 (SOLVE_LOG 4).
Models B2 (strokes ignored), B3 (every mark a letter), C (every sign+mark its own letter), 4 seeds each: no agreement (SOLVE_LOG 5-7).
Raised figures 4 5 6 7 8 = a e i o u (kept); barred signs with dots as name codes (wrong: they are doubled consonants) (SOLVE_LOG 8-9).

Model B5 (vowels fixed), 5 seeds: seed 2 reads 'intenderete', 'opera per intendere', 'potrete', 'e da credere'; other seeds fail. Variants with S04 merged into S03 fail; with vowels free one seed partial (SOLVE_LOG 10, 10b, 10c).

Pattern word in the cipher (lines 1 and 3) = 'intendere', 'intenderete'; it also stands in the clear lines of the letter. Then 'per' x10 and the rest of the key by sense from lines 1-6 only; first idea 'meglio' wrong, 'quello/quella/quale/questo' fits (SOLVE_LOG 11-12).
Key frozen (FREEZE_KEY.txt), then one decode of all 8 lines, held-out lines 7-8 included, no emendation (decode_once.py, DECODE.txt).

Separate strict judge (Claude Opus 5.5), given only the brief and the decode, scored each letter S/E/N: build lines 1-6 307/343 = 89.5%, held-out lines 7-8 81/92 = 88.0%, page 388/435 = 89.2% (S 388, E 11, N 36).
5,000 shuffled keys at seeds 20261112 and 7: 0 of 5,000 reach the real key on held-out (z 6.4, 6.3), build (z 7.9) and whole page (z 8.1) (shuffle_out.txt).

reading.md and translation.md made from the decode, nothing emended: 98 words, 10 holes (8 no-sense words, 2 code signs) and 11 one-letter slip words; read share 77/98 = 0.786 counting slips as holes (88/98 = 0.898 without). Line 4 end to line 5 start unread.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 286 tokens, 74 types, it-cinquecento order 4: reading -1.985 per letter; random keys -3.253 (z 10.6); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.309 (mean -2.327, z 33.2); annealer on the real text -2.271. Verdict: pass.

Reading review withdrawn: outcome.texts[0].reading_review was signed by the contributor's own session (Claude Opus 5.5, grade B, independent false). A contributor does not sign the reading review; the maintainer records it at merge (Dan Bourdeau, review of PR #997). Our error, the same as on fenian1885letter2, caught by our own audit. Class, read share (0.786) and figures unchanged.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.985; polyphony 0.0; 3 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.271

outcome.method_basis: The key was recovered from cipher lines 1-6 alone (annealing fixed the vowel figures; a pattern word in the cipher, 'intendere', opened the consonants), frozen, and then decoded the held-out lines 7-8 to Italian on the first pass. Caveat: 'intendere' also stands in the clear lines of the same letter, which the solver could see.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading.md: 77 of 98 words read as sense, counting as holes the 8 no-sense words, the 2 code signs and the 11 one-letter slip words; 88/98 = 0.898 if the slips are counted as read. Strict judge by letters: 388/435 = 0.892 (judge/judge.tsv).

texts.label: c. 16v, cipher lines 1-8
texts.summary: Ercole II tells Claudio that, since he will hear what has newly happened at Genoa, he is to learn all he can about the causes of the rising and how a person in code (probably the Emperor) means to punish it and settle the city, which, being Spain's ladder into Italy, he will not let fall to the French; he is to use extraordinary diligence.
texts.note: No reading review is recorded by the contributor; the maintainer records it at merge. A reading_review signed by our own assembling session (Claude Opus 5.5, grade B, independent false, 24 Nov 2026) was withdrawn on 27 Nov 2026 (our error, the same as on PR #997, caught by our own audit). Its content stays in NOTES.md under "Reader's notes". The checks were done with AI tools and no person checked each record by hand.

outcome.notes: Held-out design: lines 7-8 (60 of 276 signs, 21.7%) were not used to recover the key. Transcription by one model reader in one pass; no person has checked it. The gist's link to the Fieschi rising at Genoa (early January 1547) is from general knowledge, not checked in a source.
